metadata.file_name: 48. Pan & Cutumisu. (2022). Using machine learning to predict UK and Japanese secondary students' life satisfaction in PISA 2018.pdf
metadata.title: Using machine learning to predict UK and Japanese secondary students' life satisfaction in PISA 2018

design_fields.q1_rationale: Plausible values handling is not applicable because the dependent variable is the PISA 2018 life satisfaction scale score derived from student self-reports, and the paper does not describe using PV-based achievement scaling.
design_fields.q2_rationale: Matching text-readable full PDF has no explicit statement that ILSA sampling weights were omitted; weight references concern model parameters, outcome scaling, data variables or class/pixel weighting, not demonstrated sample-weight use.
design_fields.q3_rationale: The study uses student-level models without mentioning any multilevel modelling or consideration of school clustering.
design_fields.q4_rationale: The study performed only internal validation using nested cross-validation, which does not qualify as validation beyond the estimation sample.
design_fields._pdf_matched: 48. Pan & Cutumisu. (2022). Using machine learning to predict UK and Japanese secondary students' life satisfaction in PISA 2018.pdf
design_fields.q4b_note: LLM (gpt-5.4-nano): “Two supervised ML models, random forest (RF) and k-­nearest neighbours (KNN), were developed based on the UK data and the Japan data in PISA 2018.” / “both models yielded better performance on the UK data than on the Japanese data”
design_fields._q2_audit: Source checked; original extraction rationale: The study explicitly states that it did not apply sampling weights in the analysis.
